query Open Targets credible sets

Source: R/coloc-query.R
query_ot.Rd

This function takes an input credible set, uses that to define a region of interest, and searches for Open Targets credible sets that may overlap - ie contain at least one snp within the region +/- window. The resulting list of Open Targets credible sets may then be colocalised with the index credible set using the coloc_query() function.

Usage

query_ot(
  cs,
  window = 1e+05,
  type = c("all", "gwas", "qtl"),
  extra = c("traitFromSource", "pubmedId")
)

Arguments

cs

an index data.frame containing columns "chr" and "pos", for a single chromosome. chr may be numeric or character, eg 6, "6" or "X". Credible sets returned by query_ot() can be used directly.

window

numeric value saying how far outside the index credible set we should search. Given that only overlapping credible sets can show colocalisation there is no reason to set this particularly large. The default, 1e+5, has been adequate in all our tests.

type

all, gwas or qtl. Depending on your use call, you may wish to colocalise against all study types in the Open Targets dataset, just gwas datasets (you want to colocalise with human level traits eg to look for pleiotropy) or qtl datasets (you want to colocalise with molecular datasets eg to nominate causal genes).

extra

extra columns from the Open Targets manifest

Value

a list of credible sets with an attribute "annot" containing a data.frame where one row per element in the list describes the annotation of the list (most importantly, studyId).

Details

The Open Targets credible sets are stored in 200 files, each covering a contiguous block of the genome. By default, query_ot() downloads only the file(s) overlapping the query region (typically one or two, ~15 MB each) to the cache dir, and reuses them in later queries. To download everything up front (eg before working on HPC compute nodes without internet access), use ot_fetch().

Files are kept in the directory given by options(coloc.cache_dir = "path/to/dir"), so they persist between R sessions. Setting this is strongly recommended: otherwise a temporary directory is used, and files are downloaded again in every session. See coloc-options.

A few Open Targets credible sets include variants on alt or patch contigs (eg 17_KI270857v1_alt_811563_C_G). These are returned as Open Targets provides them, with pos set to NA. Because they cannot match variants on the primary chromosomes, their posterior probability counts against colocalisation, so query_ot() warns when it finds them: assess any lack of colocalisation with those credible sets carefully.

See also

coloc_query(), ot_fetch()

Author

Chris Wallace, Jeffrey Pullin

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
q <- data.table(chr = 6,
   pos = c(90279406, 90280331, 90281412, 90276601, 90288603, 90286261),
   snp = c("6_90279406_G_C", "6_90280331_G_A", "6_90281412_A_T",
           "6_90276601_A_G", "6_90288603_A_G", "6_90286261_C_G"),
   PP = c(0.675, 0.0747, 0.0702, 0.0505, 0.0422, 0.0412))

ot <- query_ot(q)
out <- coloc_query(q, ot)

out[out$PP.H4 > 0 & out$studyType != "gwas",]
} # }
